tooling: any OpenAI-compatible client; curl against POST {base}/chat/completions
chaining: pairs with a free-standing agent; the undocumented rate ceiling is the scarce link, because a retry loop is needed and the ceiling it loops against is not published

limits.value: unpublished. One 429 with retry_after 1 was observed on codestral-latest on 2026-10-22 after the same call answered; no rate-limit header is returned
free token (issued at dash.llm7.io): 1 request per second, 60 requests per minute, 250 requests per hour; the vendor publishes no keyless row
100,000 tokens per 24 hours, input plus output, on the free token

free_tier.stated: no key required for the ids probed; /v1/models lists 68 ids, none with a zero price
free_tier.notes: the catalogue carries a per-model pricing object in USD per 1M tokens and every one is above zero, which makes the free access a quota rather than a price

limits_note: no rate-limit header was returned on a live call, and the ceiling was not probed by provoking 429s, which would spend an allowance belonging to someone else's service.

identity_cost.detail: no Authorization header sent and none required for the calls that answered.

reliability_note: one id was refused with 429 'Rate limit exceeded. Retry after 1 seconds' in the second run after answering in the first, eight minutes apart
confidence_note: four ids were called twice. The answer rate is third-party; No quota is published, so the ceiling is measured only as 'it answered now'.

records.error_run2: {"message": "Rate limit exceeded. Retry after 1 seconds.", "type": "rate_limit_error", "param": null, "code": "rate_limit_exceeded", "retry_after": 1}

probe.timing_note: latency_ms and ttft_ms were taken from two different requests by the original instrument, so this record carried a row where ttft_ms exceeded latency_ms, which cannot happen on one call. The row is corrected from a re-probe on 2026-10-22T04:38:22Z with probe3.py, which derives both fields from one streaming request. The tps figures were always computed inside a single call and are unchanged.

evidence.proved: nemotron-3-nano:30b answered 200 with the model echoed and the needle present, 67 completion tokens, 672 ms in run 1 and 631 ms in run 2; codestral-latest answered in run 1 and returned 429 rate_limit_exceeded in run 2

68 model ids each carrying a pricing object with input, output and cached_input in USD per 1M tokens; no id is priced at zero; glm-5.3 and deepseek-v4-flash:0731 are listed, while the two slugs the sweep sent, GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, are absent
the free-token limits are 1 request per second, 60 per minute, 250 per hour and 100,000 tokens per day
evidence.quote: Free token access is limited to 100,000 tokens/day with 250 r/h, 60 r/m, and 1 r/s.

evidence.proved: the first-party limits table for /v1/chat/completions lists a Free token row (1 per second, 60 per minute, 250 per hour) and a Pro row, and no anonymous or keyless row
the documented free token is issued at dash.llm7.io against an email address; the keyless call is not documented
evidence.quote: we will store your email address (and minimal related metadata) for the purpose of issuing, managing, and securing those tokens, enforcing rate limits, and preventing abuse.

evidence.proved: one POST with no Authorization header for nemotron-3-nano:30b answered 200 and echoed model nemotron-3-nano:30b; content was empty with a reasoning field and finish_reason length at max_tokens 64; no rate-limit header was returned (headers: server cloudflare, x-llm-gateway-cache MISS, x-request-id)

notes: The cleanest available ordering in the sweep: nemotron-3-nano:30b measured 53.12 and 86.43 tok/s and codestral-latest 127.60 and a 429. The two ids recorded as listed-but-refusing, GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, do not appear in /v1/models at all; the catalogue carries glm-5.3 and deepseek-v4-flash:0731, so a 400 on the unpublished slug proves nothing about the catalogue's honesty.
